# Claude vs an open-weight model on HA20 and SSADH deficiency (D-10)

*Pre-registration §7.5 (O5, secondary). Generated by `analysis/openweight/report.py` from `analysis/openweight/summary_<d>.json`, `analysis/openweight/o2/`, `analysis/six_disease/o2/`, `runs/ow-<d>/`, `analysis/openweight/gatekeeper_compare.json` and the memorization-probe summaries. Run date 2026-10-21. HA20 is a development disease (D-18); SSADH deficiency is not.*

## 1. What ran

- **Open-weight model:** `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 2026-09-10 checkpoint) through `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, provider pinned to `deepinfra/fp8` with fallbacks off. Every final attempt was served by DeepInfra|deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash.
- **Claude:** the frozen six-disease run (`pv1-ha20`, `pv1-ssadh`), Claude Code helper agents (D-17, D-20).
- **Same inputs:** the same papers (85 HA20, 40 SSADH), the same launch prompt (copied from the pv1 helpers), and the same instruction, schema and rules files, unchanged from the frozen commit (`ef3133e`) and the D-38 per-disease copies. Hashes are in each manifest.
- **Same scoring:** both runs went through the same span check, reconciliation (merge policy v4), VariantValidator normalization and O2 harness (ClinVar snapshot 2026-10-19), with no gatekeeper filtering on either side.
- **Spend:** between **$16.34** and **$20.35**, billed to OpenRouter, not the award (`BUDGET.md`). The host reported $10.25 (HA20) and $5.54 (SSADH) for final attempts, plus $0.55 for the 5 failed attempts that logged usage; 10 failed attempts stopped before logging any. The key's usage rose $1.07 → $21.42 ($20.35) over the runs, but the key is shared with other projects in the same environment (`DECISIONS.md`, 2026-10-21), so that rise is an upper bound.

## 4. How the scaffolds differed

Stated as the plan requires (§7.5). Claude's helpers ran in Claude Code; the open-weight model ran in `pipeline/extract/openweight/agent.py`.

- **No shell.** The open-weight loop had file tools only: read, grep, glob, write and edit, with the same read and write limits. Claude's helpers also had a shell, which they used for small checking scripts, and Claude Code's own system prompt.
- **Harness fixes during the run** (approved by Dr. Lin, 2026-10-21; `DECISIONS.md`, D-10 OpenRouter entry):
  - retries after dropped connections and 5xx errors;
  - v2: a write to a `.json` file reports whether it parses. The frozen instructions ask for that check, and Claude's helpers made it with the shell;
  - v3: a reply cut off at the output limit is followed by a request to resume.
- **Which harness version made each final output:** HA20 v1 72, v2 10, v3 3; SSADH v2 39, v3 1. The resume request (v3) was never needed: 0 resumes.
- **Failed attempts:** 13 HA20 papers and 1 SSADH paper were re-run from a clean start. The failures were dropped connections, one output that did not parse, and four replies cut off before any file was written. Each failed attempt is kept in `runs/ow-<d>/failed_attempts/`.
- **Retried calls in final attempts:** HA20 36, SSADH 17.

## 5. Reading the results

- **Provenance:** every value Claude asserted had a quote found in the paper. The open-weight model gave no quote for 3.6% (HA20) and 3.0% (SSADH) of its values. When it gave one, the quote was almost always in the paper.
- **Variants:** the two models found largely the same target-gene variants (§3). Claude's HGVS recall against ClinVar was higher on HA20 and about the same on SSADH; the denominators are small and the intervals overlap.
- **Phenotypes:** the open-weight model wrote 54% (HA20) and 86% (SSADH) as many phenotypic-feature rows as Claude. Checklist cells marked observed or excluded were slightly more numerous for the open-weight model.
- **Cost:** per paper, the median open-weight cost was 1/15 (HA20) and 1/18 (SSADH) of Claude's estimated cost. Counted with failed attempts, the open-weight runs cost $16.34 to $20.35 for 125 papers (§1), against Claude's $154.21 estimate (1/9.4 to 1/7.6).
- **Time:** the median open-weight paper took 7.3× (HA20) and 6.7× (SSADH) as long as Claude's.
- **Support (gatekeeper, §6):** the same Claude gatekeeper judged 8.6% (HA20) and 6.1% (SSADH) of the open-weight model's claims unsupported, against 0.2% and 0.4% of Claude's. Most of the gap is claims with no quote, but claims with a quote were also judged unsupported more often: 11× (HA20), 5× (SSADH) Claude's rate.
- **Not yet measured:** whether a value is right as a person reads it. That is the blinded audit (§2).
- **Scope:** two diseases, one open-weight model, one provider. These are not general findings.

## 6. Gatekeeper reading on both runs

Approved by Dr. Lin on 2026-10-21 (gatekeeper line; `DECISIONS.md`). The frozen gatekeeper v4 judged the open-weight run's claims with the same instructions, launch prompt and helper setup as the pv1 runs: Claude Code helpers, one per chunk, reading only the instructions, the claims and the paper. Claims are numbered and classed by the same prep script. Model claims only (the ones a helper judges); exact 95% intervals.

| Measure | HA20 Claude | HA20 open-weight | SSADH Claude | SSADH open-weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model claims judged | 23,129 | 18,084 | 9,759 | 10,372 |
| Supported | 22,683 | 15,250 | 9,480 | 9,020 |
| Partially supported | 400 | 1,240 | 242 | 715 |
| Unsupported | 46 | 1,563 | 37 | 637 |
| Span not found | 0 | 31 | 0 | 0 |
| **Unsupported rate** | **0.20% (0.15–0.27)** | **8.64% (8.24–9.06)** | **0.38% (0.27–0.52)** | **6.14% (5.69–6.62)** |
| Anything but supported | 1.93% (1.75–2.11) | 15.67% (15.14–16.21) | 2.86% (2.54–3.21) | 13.04% (12.39–13.70) |
| Claims with an empty quote | 0 | 1,503 | 0 | 591 |
| … judged unsupported | 0 | 1,185 | 0 | 438 |
| Unsupported rate, claims with a quote | 0.20% (0.15–0.27) | 2.28% (2.06–2.52) | 0.38% (0.27–0.52) | 2.03% (1.76–2.33) |
| Papers with an unsupported claim | 15 | 71 | 7 | 37 |

Fields with most unsupported claims:

- HA20 Claude: `variants.gene_symbol_as_stated` 17; `phenotypic_features.status` 9; `individuals.clinical_diagnosis_basis` 5; `phenotypic_features.feature_text_as_stated` 3
- HA20 open-weight: `phenotype_checklist.status` 682; `individuals.is_proband` 477; `phenotypic_features.status` 79; `phenotypic_features.severity_or_detail` 69
- SSADH Claude: `variants.gene_symbol_as_stated` 16; `individuals.source_reference_in_review` 3; `variants.transcript_as_stated` 3; `variants.genomic_coordinates_as_stated` 3
- SSADH open-weight: `individuals.is_proband` 323; `phenotypic_features.status` 78; `phenotypic_features.severity_or_detail` 76; `variants.gene_symbol_as_stated` 42

How to read it:

- **The judge is Claude.** A Claude gatekeeper judging a Claude extraction and a non-Claude extraction may not be neutral. The blinded human audit (§2) is what settles support; this table is the gatekeeper's reading only.
- **Empty quotes.** Claude's helpers left no asserted value without a quote. In a handful of pv1 papers that was after a repair-only resume of a helper that had left quotes empty (`reports/six_disease_run_findings.md`). The open-weight run had no repair pass. That is a scaffold difference, stated here as §7.5 asks.
- **Empty quotes were not judged the same way by every helper.** Gatekeeper v4 says a value needs its own quote. Most helpers judged an empty-quote claim unsupported (1,185 of 1,503 HA20, 438 of 591 SSADH). Some judged it against the quote on the same row and called it supported (236 HA20, 144 SSADH) or partially supported. So the open-weight unsupported rate is, if anything, a little low.
- **Quotes not in the paper:** 48 HA20 and 8 SSADH model claims had a quote the span check did not find (the rest of §2's count are bookkeeping fields). Helpers marked 31 and 0 of them span not found and judged the others against near-matching text. Gatekeeper v4 tells helpers that a script has confirmed every quote verbatim; that held for every Claude claim but not for these, because the prep script does not drop them. The verdicts stand in this table; §2 still counts these quotes as not found.
- **Common open-weight failures, from the helpers' reasons:** `is_proband` = false with no quote; checklist statuses with no quote; a gene symbol quoted from a background sentence rather than the person's test result; an age at examination or presentation given as an onset age; parents' variant fields quoted from the proband's sentence; hedged findings ("possible", "suspected") recorded as observed.

## 7. Memorization probe on both models

Exploratory (§7.4.3). The same 180 papers and probe items as the Claude side (WS5), sent to the open-weight model with no tools and the items inline; the Claude helpers read the same items from a file. Run 2026-10-21, 12 calls, $0.05 on the OpenRouter key. Scored by the same script against the pv1 extraction, never against ClinVar or OMIM. Full tables: `analysis/bias/memorization/scores_summary.md` (Claude) and `openweight_scores_summary.md`.

| Measure, all 180 papers | Claude | Open-weight |
|---|---|---|
| Closed-book answers marked specific | 4 | 0 |
| … marked guess | 145 | 41 |
| … marked none | 31 | 139 |
| Papers with a variant hit | 4 | 3 |
| Variants given (hits) | 12 (4) | 13 (3) |
| Phenotype terms given / matching the paper | 493 / 233 | 103 / 25 |
| Completions with a run of 8+ words from the paper | 3 | 0 |
| Longest run from the paper, max (words) | 11 | 7 |

- Neither model showed recall of these papers' variants: a handful of variant hits each, the kind a guess from the title or the gene's best-known variant gives.
- The open-weight model more often answered "none". Claude guessed more phenotypes, and more of them matched the paper, which is what general knowledge of the disease predicts; it is not evidence of recall of the paper.
- The strata (before or after a training cutoff) were set from Claude's cutoff. The open-weight checkpoint's cutoff is not known here, so its strata carry no meaning.
- This probe does not explain the support gap in §6: neither model reproduced the papers' variants, and the longest run of the papers' own words in a completion was 11 words (Claude) and 7 (open-weight).
